message.content:
The total number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of **10⁴³**.  

This figure comes from combinatorial estimates that take into account all the ways pieces can be arranged on the board, the constraints of the rules (e.g., no more than eight pawns per side, castling rights, en‑passant possibilities, etc.). While the exact count is still an open problem, the consensus estimate is roughly \(10^{43}\) possible positions.
